extracted.intended_audience: academics, medical professionals, and applicants for university prizes, scholarships, and teaching appointments (readers of Nature, 1907)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal conditions for submitting prize essays/dissertations, applying for scholarships, and applying for university/technical teaching appointments (eligibility, formatting, deadlines, anonymity, and disqualification rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Astley Cooper Prize — subject and award
rubrics_metrics.description: Triennial Prize of Three Hundred Pounds awarded for the best Essay or Treatise on 'The Physiology of Digestion, Gastric and Intestinal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition open to everyone except the staffs of Guy's and St. Thomas's Hospitals and their relations. The Trustees will consider publication of the successful essay in the 'Guy's Hospital Reports'; publication there will not preclude the author from publishing elsewhere upon obtaining permission. For particulars apply to Sir Coomer Perrys, M.D., Guy's Hospital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astley Cooper Prize — authorship and language
rubrics_metrics.description: The essay must not be the production of two or more authors; entries must be written in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-author submissions only; joint authorship disallowed. Ensure manuscript is in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astley Cooper Prize — submission anonymity and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each essay or treatise must be distinguished by a motto, and be accompanied by a sealed envelope containing the true name and address of the writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enclose a sealed envelope with the author's name/address; do not put identifying information on the essay itself except the motto. None of the envelopes will be opened except that accompanying the successful treatise (i.e., submissions are adjudicated anonymously).

rubrics_metrics.name: Astley Cooper Prize — submission deadline and address
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be sent to Guy's Hospital, addressed to the Physiology and Sarcom. (sic), on or before January 1, 1910.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the stated deadline and addressing instructions; late entries will not comply. For further conditions, contact the named official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rogers Prize (1908) — subject, eligibility, and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Prize open to all members of the medical profession in the United Kingdom for the best essay or dissertation setting forth the results of original investigations made by the candidate on any medical pathological subject during the preceding two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work must report original investigations carried out by the candidate within the two years prior to submission. Membership of the UK medical profession is required for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rogers Prize — use of previously published papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates will be permitted to present papers published during the preceding ... years as the dissertation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously published papers (from the permitted preceding period) may be submitted as the candidate's dissertation; check the exact allowed preceding period in full particulars (page text truncated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rogers Prize — format and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The essay or dissertation, by preference typewritten or printed, must be sent not later than May 1, 1908, addressed to the Clerk of Committees, University of London, South Kensington, S.W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer typewritten/printed copies for clarity. Observe the submission deadline and address precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrance Medical Scholarships — evidence and post-award requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarships in Arts or Science open to competition to men and women will be awarded to candidates who give evidence of a high standard of proficiency. Successful candidates will be required to enter for the full medical curriculum in the University and the Infirmary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate high proficiency (by the selection mechanism/examination). Awardees are expected to undertake the full medical course as a condition of holding the scholarship. Applications to be sent by stated deadline to the Registrar for particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application forms, testimonials, and postal requirements (LCC Assistant Mistress example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should be made on Form 40 H.G., to be obtained from the Clerk of the Council's Education Offices; they must be returned by the stated deadline and be accompanied by copies of three testimonials of recent date. Postal applicants should enclose a stamped and addressed envelope for return of the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and use the prescribed form. Attach three recent testimonials. If applying by post for the application form, include a stamped addressed envelope. Meet the deadline and follow the exact submission address instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of canvassing
rubrics_metrics.description: Canvassing, either directly or indirectly, will be considered a disqualification for appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not solicit support, lobby, or otherwise canvass in connection with the application; any such activity risks automatic disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position-specific qualification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Several advertised posts require specified qualifications: e.g., instructor of metal-work must hold the first-class certificate of the City and Guilds of London Institute or equivalent; lecturer in chemistry must have knowledge of agricultural chemistry; applicants for vice-principal should have special knowledge of surveying and bookkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you meet the stated professional/technical qualifications and any preferred additional skills (e.g., ability to teach workshop mathematics, engineering drawing). State relevant credentials in the application and supply proof where requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and where to obtain particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for exams, scholarships, appointments, and courses must be sent by specified dates to the named officials (e.g., Registrar, Secretary, Principal). Full particulars and prospectuses are obtainable from the named officers or offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the named contact for full particulars and prospectuses (often available post free on application). Strictly observe the listed deadlines (dates like August 15, September 16, May 1, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship/exam competition conditions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrance/examination competitions (scholarships, examinations for degrees) have specified dates, values, and conditions (e.g., number of scholarships, value in pounds, requirement to undertake a specified curriculum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review each competition's stated scope (who may compete), value, obligations if successful, and exact dates for examination or application; inquire of the Registrar for full details.
